request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1.)

tools.name: get_fold_detail
tools.description: Get the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown for a completed experiment run. Use this to compare fold-level consistency between runs.

output.text:
**Chosen run: 1 (random forest, all features, class weights).** Confidence is about 0.55.

| Run | Model | PR-AUC mean | SD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Random forest | 0.705 | 0.065 |
| 2 | LightGBM | 0.733 | 0.056 |
| 3 | LightGBM | 0.701 | 0.079 |

- **Run 2 vs run 1:** Run 2 is ahead on all five folds, by 0.012 to 0.044. Its mean gain is about 0.028, which is less than one fold SD (0.056 to 0.065). The decision rule says to keep the simpler model unless the complex one wins by more than one SD. So the rule picks the random forest. The consistent fold-level win is why I'm not more confident. Reasonable reviewers could pick run 2.
- **Run 3:** It is the weakest and the most variable (SD 0.079). It has no case for selection.
- **Fold difficulty:** All three runs find fold 3 hardest (about 0.60 to 0.65) and folds 1 and 4 easiest. This looks like a property of the data split, not of any one model.
- **Results that look too good:** None do. PR-AUC of about 0.70 and precision@50 of about 0.75 are plausible against a 9.35% base rate. The ROC-AUC of about 0.94 is high but is the less informative metric under this imbalance.
- **Caveats:**
  - The label origin is undocumented, so these scores measure agreement with a suspicion flag, not detection of confirmed fraud.
  - Run 2 uses the `agent` features. I can't tell from this data whether they leak the label, so check that before relying on run 2.
  - The audit queue is about 100 providers, but only precision@50 was reported, so queue-sized performance is unverified.
- **Further search:** No rounds remain, and more search is unlikely to change the choice. The gap between the top two runs is smaller than the noise across folds.
